title: Beyond a Single Sentiment Score: Topical and Affective Dimensions of Emoji Meaning on Twitter
Beyond a Single Sentiment Score: Topical and Affective Dimensions of Emoji Meaning on Twitter
summary: The paper argues that representing an emoji by a single sentiment scalar collapses two dissociable dimensions of meaning: how topically coherent its contexts are and how affectively dispersed its crowd-sourced ratings are. It introduces 'stability delta', the within-class minus between-class mean cosine similarity of all-MiniLM-L6-v2 embeddings of emoji-free tweet text, computes it for the 62 emojis with at least 15 occurrences in the Emoji Sarcasm Dataset, and correlates it with external per-emoji affect-dispersion measures. The headline result is a positive Spearman correlation with Kralj Novak sentiment variance (rho = +0.361, Holm p = 0.015, n = 59) corroborated by Ferre 2025 strongly-evoked-emotion counts (rho = +0.509, p = 0.0003, n = 47), with a saturated (>0.97 macro F1) sarcasm classifier reported only as supporting evidence.

approach: Reimplement only the C1 pipeline, because the inspected repository is the Emoji Sarcasm Dataset release, not the paper's analysis code. Clone and load the ESD Twitter partition, apply the 85% ASCII English filter, canonicalize emojis, take the first emoji as primary, build the >=15-occurrence 62-emoji panel, and encode emoji-free lowercased text with all-MiniLM-L6-v2. For each panel emoji, sample up to 100 within-emoji tweets and 500 background tweets, compute delta = W_e - B_e, join to emosent-py, and run the 59-emoji Spearman with 10,000 permutations, percentile and BCa bootstrap CIs, Holm correction over the four Kralj Novak tests, and partial Spearman controlling for emoji frequency. The final `python reproduce.py` writes `results/metrics.json`; C3 descriptive delta checks are logged as sanity evidence, while C4-C6 classifier claims and their R11-R13 requirements are out of scope for this CPU C1 reproduction.

If data is absent, git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/jsubram/Sarcasm-Detection-Using-Emoji into data/raw/esd; confirm Data/Final_Dataset_Twitter.csv exists and load it with pandas, preserving tweet order.

Run src/prepare_data.py: apply the 85% ASCII English filter to raw text, assert the exact count 16587 (or log and diagnose if off by a few), detect all emojis with the emoji library, strip U+1F3FB-U+1F3FF and U+FE0F, take the first canonical emoji as primary_emoji, build emoji-free lowercased clean_text, drop no-emoji tweets, and assert 16575 final corpus rows.

Build the analytical panel: count primary_emoji occurrences, retain emojis with count >= 15, and assert 62 emojis covering 15569 tweets; save data/processed/tweets.parquet and results/preprocess_counts.json.

Run src/embed_text.py: load SentenceTransformer('all-MiniLM-L6-v2') on CPU, encode clean_text with batch_size=64, normalize_embeddings=True, save float32 embeddings.npy aligned to the processed tweet index.

Run src/stability_delta.py with RNG seed 42: for each panel emoji in sorted codepoint order, sample up to 100 within tweets and 500 background tweets from primary_emoji != e, compute W_e as mean off-diagonal dot product, B_e as mean cross-pair dot product, delta = W_e - B_e, and save results/deltas.csv; also compute C3 sanity statistics.

Run src/kralj_novak.py: import emosent-py, inspect available per-emoji fields if names differ, canonicalize lexicon keys, match the panel, compute variance ddof=0 over (p_neg,p_neu,p_pos), and save results/kralj_novak.csv; assert n=59 matched emojis or print the unmatched list.

This proves CSV loading, filtering, emoji extraction, embedding, delta sampling, lexicon matching, and stats flow end-to-end without touching the full 16k corpus.
intermediate_checks: Dependency check: sentence-transformers, emoji, emosent-py, scipy, pandas, numpy import successfully; if emosent-py import name differs, inspect the installed package and record the callable/fields.

Dataset size check: raw DataFrame has 16859 Twitter rows; after the 85% ASCII English filter it has 16587 rows; after emoji normalization and primary-emoji extraction it has 16575 rows; after >=15-occurrence filtering it has 62 emojis covering 15569 tweets.

Emoji normalization check: no panel emoji contains U+1F3FB-U+1F3FF or U+FE0F; each row has exactly one primary_emoji; emoji-only tweets are retained with an empty clean_text if present (A6).
Embedding check: embeddings.npy shape is (16575, 384), dtype float32, and row-wise L2 norms are approximately 1.0; no NaNs.

Delta sanity check: mean delta across the 62 emojis is near 0.0766, max near +0.237, min near -0.003, and 61 of 62 deltas are positive; large deviations indicate wrong primary-emoji choice, cleaning, or background sampling.
Lexicon match check: Kralj Novak matching returns exactly 59 emojis; variance values are finite, non-negative, and computed from probability triples rather than the scalar sentiment score.

Primary correlation check: Spearman rho over 59 emojis is near +0.361, permutation p is near 0.005, Holm-adjusted p is significant and near 0.015, bootstrap CI is roughly [+0.10, +0.59], and jackknife range is roughly [+0.333, +0.412].
Sanity baseline: permuting the Kralj Novak variance labels should produce rho centered near 0 with no significant p, confirming the permutation code is not leaking the pairing.
budget_plan: CPU-only budget of about 15 minutes: 4 minutes for pip installs, repo clone, and MiniLM weight download; 1 minute for the smoke test; 8-12 minutes for full preprocessing, embedding ~16.6k short tweets with all-MiniLM-L6-v2, computing 62 deltas, and running 10k permutations plus 10k percentile/BCa bootstrap resamples on 59 points. import pandas as pd, numpy as np, re, collections, emoji as emoji_lib

df = pd.read_csv('repo/Data/Final_Dataset_Twitter.csv', dtype=str)
txt = df['Comments'].fillna('').tolist()

URL = re.compile(r'https?://\S+|www\.\S+|pic\.twitter\.com/\S+')
MENTION = re.compile(r'@\w+')

def canon(e):
    return ''.join(ch for ch in e if not (0x1F3FB <= ord(ch) <= 0x1F3FF) and ord(ch) != 0xFE0F)

def emojis_of(s):
    return [c for m in emoji_lib.emoji_list(s) if (c := canon(m['emoji']))]

def ratio(s):
    a = sum(1 for ch in s if ch.isascii() and ch.isalpha())
    d = sum(1 for ch in s if ch.isalpha())
    return a / d if d else 0.0

variants = {
    'raw': lambda s: s,
    'url_only': lambda s: URL.sub(' ', s),
    'url_mention': lambda s: MENTION.sub(' ', URL.sub(' ', s)),
    'url_hash': lambda s: URL.sub(' ', s).replace('#', ' '),
    'url_mention_hash': lambda s: MENTION.sub(' ', URL.sub(' ', s)).replace('#', ' '),
    'lower_url': lambda s: URL.sub(' ', s.lower()),
}
for name, f in variants.items():
    kept = [f(s) for s in txt if ratio(f(s)) >= 0.85]
    removed = 16859 - len(kept)
    em = [emojis_of(s) for s in kept]
    n_noemoji = sum(1 for e in em if not e)
    final = len(kept) - n_noemoji
    cnt = collections.Counter(e[0] for e in em if e)
    panel = {k: v for k, v in cnt.items() if v >= 15}
    print(f'{name:18s} removed={removed} kept={len(kept)} noemoji={n_noemoji} final={final} '
          f'panel={len(panel)} coverage={sum(panel.values())}')

    """Strip skin-tone modifiers U+1F3FB-U+1F3FF and Variation Selector-16 (A5)."""

"""Stability delta per Section 4.3, Eqs. (1)-(3) (R5, R6).

For each panel emoji e:
  Te   = tweets whose primary emoji is e; sample up to WITHIN_SAMPLE_MAX
  Bg   = 500 random tweets with primary_emoji != e (T \ Te, A2)
  We   = mean cosine over ordered pairs i != j (self-similarity excluded)
  Be   = mean cosine over the n_e x 500 cross pairs
  Delta_e = We - Be
Embeddings are the L2-normalised MiniLM vectors, so cos = dot.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import json
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent))
from src import config  # noqa: E402


def compute_deltas(embeddings: np.ndarray, corpus: pd.DataFrame, panel: dict,
                   within_max: int, between_size: int, seed: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
    emoji_col = corpus["primary_emoji"].to_numpy()
    rows = []
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    for emoji in sorted(panel):                       # sorted codepoint order for determinism
        idx = np.where(emoji_col == emoji)[0]
        n_within = min(within_max, len(idx))
        within_idx = rng.choice(idx, size=n_within, replace=False)
        bg_pool = np.where(emoji_col != emoji)[0]
        n_bg = min(between_size, len(bg_pool))
        bg_idx = rng.choice(bg_pool, size=n_bg, replace=False)

        X = embeddings[within_idx]
        Y = embeddings[bg_idx]
        G = X @ X.T
        n = X.shape[0]
        if n > 1:
            w_sim = (G.sum() - np.trace(G)) / (n * (n - 1))   # ordered pairs i != j (R6)
        else:
            w_sim = float("nan")
        b_sim = float((X @ Y.T).mean()) if n and Y.shape[0] else float("nan")

        rows.append({
            "emoji": emoji,
            "occurrences": int(panel[emoji]),
            "n_within_sampled": int(n),
            "n_background": int(Y.shape[0]),
            "within_sim": float(w_sim),
            "between_sim": float(b_sim),
            "delta": float(w_sim - b_sim),
        })
    return pd.DataFrame(rows)

    d = deltas["delta"].to_numpy()
    top = deltas.sort_values("delta", ascending=False).iloc[0]
    bot = deltas.sort_values("delta").iloc[0]

"""Statistical battery: Spearman + permutation p, percentile/BCa bootstrap CIs,
jackknife, partial Spearman, Kendall tau and Holm correction (R8, R9, R10).

All randomness is seeded (A8). Permutation p is two-sided empirical:
p = (1 + #{|rho_perm| >= |rho_obs|}) / (n_perm + 1).
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import json
import math
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from scipy import stats

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent))
from src import config  # noqa: E402

Z_LO = stats.norm.ppf(0.025)
Z_HI = stats.norm.ppf(0.975)


def _spearman(a: np.ndarray, b: np.ndarray) -> float:
    rho = stats.spearmanr(a, b).statistic
    return float(rho)


def permutation_p(delta: np.ndarray, y: np.ndarray, rho_obs: float, n_perm: int, seed: int) -> float:
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    count = 0
    for _ in range(n_perm):
        perm = rng.permutation(y)
        rho_p = _spearman(delta, perm)
        if abs(rho_p) >= abs(rho_obs):
            count += 1
    return (1 + count) / (n_perm + 1)


def percentile_bca_ci(delta: np.ndarray, y: np.ndarray, rho_obs: float, n_boot: int, seed: int):
    """Paired percentile + BCa bootstrap CI for Spearman rho (A8)."""
    n = len(delta)
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    boot = np.empty(n_boot)
    for b in range(n_boot):
        idx = rng.integers(0, n, size=n)
        boot[b] = _spearman(delta[idx], y[idx])
    ok = np.isfinite(boot)
    boot = boot[ok]
    lo_pct, hi_pct = np.percentile(boot, [2.5, 97.5])

    # BCa bias-correction
    frac = float(np.mean(boot < rho_obs))
    frac = min(max(frac, 1.0 / (2 * len(boot))), 1 - 1.0 / (2 * len(boot)))
    z0 = stats.norm.ppf(frac)

    # BCa acceleration from the jackknife
    jack = np.array([_spearman(np.delete(delta, i), np.delete(y, i)) for i in range(n)])
    jmean = jack.mean()
    diff = jmean - jack
    denom = 6.0 * (np.sum(diff ** 2) ** 1.5)
    accel = float(np.sum(diff ** 3) / denom) if denom > 0 else 0.0

    def _alpha(z):
        return stats.norm.cdf(z0 + (z0 + z) / (1.0 - accel * (z0 + z)))

    a1, a2 = _alpha(Z_LO), _alpha(Z_HI)
    bca_lo, bca_hi = np.percentile(boot, [100 * a1, 100 * a2])
    return {
        "percentile_ci": [float(lo_pct), float(hi_pct)],
        "bca_ci": [float(bca_lo), float(bca_hi)],
        "bca_bias_z0": float(z0),
        "bca_acceleration": accel,
        "bca_alpha1": float(a1),
        "bca_alpha2": float(a2),
        "boot_mean": float(np.mean(boot)),
        "n_boot_valid": int(len(boot)),
    }


def partial_spearman(delta: np.ndarray, y: np.ndarray, freq: np.ndarray) -> dict:
    """Partial Spearman controlling for emoji frequency via rank residuals (R10)."""
    r_d = stats.rankdata(delta)
    r_y = stats.rankdata(y)
    r_f = stats.rankdata(freq)

    def _resid(r_v):
        X = np.column_stack([np.ones_like(r_f), r_f])
        beta, *_ = np.linalg.lstsq(X, r_v, rcond=None)
        return r_v - X @ beta

    res_d = _resid(r_d)
    res_y = _resid(r_y)
    pearson = float(np.corrcoef(res_d, res_y)[0, 1])
    spearman_res = float(stats.pearsonr(res_d, res_y).statistic)
    return {"partial_rho_pearson_on_rank_residuals": pearson,
            "partial_rho_spearman_on_rank_residuals": float(stats.spearmanr(res_d, res_y).statistic),
            "_pearson_note": spearman_res}


def holm(pvals: dict) -> dict:
    """Holm step-down adjustment; returns adjusted p in the original key order."""
    items = sorted(pvals.items(), key=lambda kv: kv[1])
    m = len(items)
    adj = {}
    running = 0.0
    for rank, (key, p) in enumerate(items):
        val = (m - rank) * p
        running = max(running, val)
        adj[key] = float(min(1.0, running))
    return adj

        "sentiment_score": merged["sentiment_score"].to_numpy(dtype=float),
        "p_pos": merged["p_pos"].to_numpy(dtype=float),

    family = {}
    for name, y in targets.items():

target.statement: Stability delta of an emoji correlates positively with the variance of its Kralj Novak (2015) crowd-sourced sentiment distribution across the 59 matched emojis; this is the paper's designated primary test and survives Holm correction across the four-test family.
target.dataset: Emoji Sarcasm Dataset (ESD) Twitter partition + Kralj Novak et al. (2015) emoji sentiment lexicon (via emosent-py)
target.table_ref: Table 2, row 'Delta vs. Kralj Novak variance (primary)', column rho

tolerance.why: Rule 3: the target is a bounded rank correlation (Spearman rho) computed on a small emoji panel (n = 59), and the paper prints it as a fraction (0.361), not a percentage, so the band is 0.02 absolute. Rule 1 does not apply because the paper gives bootstrap CIs and a jackknife range, not a standard deviation over repeated runs, and Rule 2 does not apply because this is not an accuracy-like % on a 2,000+ example test set.

audit_summary: C1 was reproduced end-to-end on the full ESD Twitter partition with the emosent-py lexicon: 16,859 raw rows -> 16,587 after the 85% ASCII filter (272 removed) -> 16,575-tweet corpus -> 62-emoji panel (15,571 tweets; paper 15,569) -> 59 matched emojis. The computed Spearman rho is +0.3805 (10,000-permutation p=0.0032, Holm p=0.0059), within the contract's 0.02 band of the paper's +0.361; the percentile/BCa CIs, Kendall tau, jackknife and null check are all reported. The stability-delta formula, MiniLM embeddings, KN variance target, permutation/bootstrap battery and partial-Spearman control follow the paper; the only notable fidelity gaps are the 2-tweet panel-coverage discrepancy, the ambiguous Holm family (R9), and partial rho +0.391 vs +0.370 (R10). C2 and C4-C8 (including all classifiers and VADER) were not attempted, so R11-R13 and the VADER part of R2 are missing/partial. Paper constants (0.361, C3 descriptives) appear in config only for pass/fail comparison, not to generate the reported metric, and no scale-down was used.

requirement_check.evidence: prepare_data applies the 85% ASCII-alphabetic test after URL stripping (A11); clean rerun gives raw=16859, removed=272, kept=16587, matching R1 exactly.
MiniLM embeddings are built from emoji-free clean_text, but VADER scoring (C7) was not implemented; the sentence-embedding half of R2 is satisfied.
62 emojis are retained at >=15 occurrences from a 16,575-tweet corpus, but panel coverage is 15,571 vs the paper's 15,569 (2-tweet emoji-detection/parsing gap, disclosed in A12).
sentence-transformers all-MiniLM-L6-v2 is used; embeddings are asserted shape (16575, 384) and L2-normalised (norms ~1.0).
Primary emoji = first canonical emoji (A1); up to 100 within-emoji tweets are sampled; 500 background tweets are sampled from primary_emoji != e with seed 42.
within_sim = (sum(X X^T)-trace)/(n(n-1)) over ordered i!=j pairs; between_sim = mean(X Y^T) over the n x 500 cross pairs; delta = within - between.
emosent-py counts are normalised to p_neg,p_neu,p_pos; kn_variance = np.var(triple, ddof=0), i.e. variance of the three probabilities, not the scalar sentiment score.
10,000 two-sided permutation p plus 10,000-resample percentile and BCa bootstrap CIs are implemented and reported (permutation p=0.0032; BCa CI [+0.1227,+0.5952]).

Delta-vs-KN-variance is treated as primary and Holm is applied, but the four-test family is the implementer's four delta-vs-KN tests (variance, score, p_pos, p_neg), not necessarily the paper's partially named mixed KN family; both asymptotic and permutation Holm p are reported (0.0059/0.0064) and the primary survives.
Partial Spearman controlling for frequency is reported as +0.3914 (rank-residual Pearson; +0.3959 alternative), close to but not the paper's +0.370.
No sarcasm classifiers were trained or evaluated; the five-fold GEMA/BERTweet/RoBERTa comparison (C4-C6) was out of the implemented scope.
No classifier pipeline exists, so within-fold centroid-distance recomputation was not implemented.
VADER was not run; C7 and the VADER leakage check were not attempted.
